key_insight: A DMRG-prepared MPS can be encoded efficiently up to a logistic-growth threshold, then finished with scheduled probabilistic imaginary-time evolution to avoid very deep circuits.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid workflow reduces quantum ground-state preparation cost by shifting hard optimization and state-quality estimation into classical preprocessing and by truncating the expensive encoding tail.
method: Use DMRG to obtain an MPS for the target N-site ground state.
Load the MPS with an optimization-free MPD encoding circuit until the central-bond Schmidt-rank inflection point L*.
Apply deterministically scheduled PITE to suppress the remaining excited-state error using energy, gap, and overlap estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on the spin-1/2 staggered-field Heisenberg chain showing that stopping at L* avoids very deep encoding circuits and reduces PITE post-selection overhead.
watch_item: The approach relies on reliable classical estimates of the ground-state energy, effective gap, and reference overlap, which may be difficult for larger or less well-behaved systems.
paper_title: Overcoming the Matrix-Product-State Encoding Barrier via DMRG-Guided Probabilistic Imaginary-Time Evolution
